# Air pollution — causes, effects, and control

## 1. Introduction
Opening frame for **Air pollution — causes** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Environmental Issues fill pass.

## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Air pollution — causes
### effects
### and control

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

Air pollution is the addition of harmful substances to the atmosphere — gases (CO, SO2, NOx), particulates (PM2.5, PM10) and secondary products (photochemical smog, acid rain). Sources are combustion, industry and vehicles; effects range from respiratory disease to acid rain and global climate change. Control combines technology (filters, converters), fuel policy and law.

## 3. Classified tables

Tables carry examples in every classification and characteristics row, ≤ 12 rows, and each is referenced from the body text (§3.3).

**Concept flow — from source to control (study in this order)**

| Step | Concept | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Primary pollutants emitted directly | CO from vehicles; SO2 from coal; PM from dust and diesel |
| 2 | Secondary pollutants formed in air | Ozone and PAN in photochemical smog; H2SO4 in acid rain |
| 3 | Effects on health | Asthma, bronchitis, heart disease; PM2.5 reaches deep lung tissue |
| 4 | Effects on environment | Acid rain damages lakes and forests; smog damages crops |
| 5 | Control at source | Electrostatic precipitators, scrubbers, catalytic converters, cleaner fuels |
| 6 | Control by policy | Emission norms (Euro/BS standards), lead-free petrol, air-quality monitoring |

**Major air pollutants — source and effect**

| Pollutant | Main source | Main harm |
|---|---|---|
| Carbon monoxide (CO) | Incomplete combustion in engines | Binds haemoglobin — carbon monoxide poisoning, suffocation |
| Sulphur dioxide (SO2) | Coal-burning power plants, smelters | Acid rain; respiratory irritation |
| Nitrogen oxides (NOx) | Vehicle engines, high-temperature combustion | Smog and acid rain; lung inflammation |
| Particulates (PM2.5/PM10) | Diesel, dust, construction, burning biomass | Deep-lung and cardiac damage; visibility loss |
| Ozone (ground-level, O3) | Secondary — sunlight + NOx + hydrocarbons | Photochemical smog; crop damage, eye irritation |
| Lead | Old petrol, battery recycling | Neurotoxic — learning impairment in children |

**Control technologies — what each device removes**

| Device / measure | Where used | What it removes |
|---|---|---|
| Electrostatic precipitator | Power-plant chimneys | Charged particles attracted to plates — up to 99% of particulates |
| Scrubber | Industrial stacks | SO2 and other gases washed out by lime-water spray |
| Catalytic converter | Vehicle exhausts | Converts CO, NOx and unburnt hydrocarbons to CO2, N2 and water — needs lead-free petrol |
| Fuel policy | Cities, refineries | Low-sulphur and unleaded fuel; CNG for buses |
| Standards and monitoring | National level | Emission norms (BS/Euro), AQI public reporting |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example — why lead killed catalytic converters.** A catalytic converter uses platinum-group catalysts to finish the combustion of CO and NOx. Lead in old petrol coats the catalyst surface in weeks and destroys it — which is why unleaded petrol was a precondition for converter-based emission norms everywhere. One pollutant (lead) had to be removed to control three others.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Pollutant table: CO (haemoglobin affinity → death), SO2/NOx (acid rain), particulates (respiratory disease), CFCs (ozone), lead (nervous system) — one effect each.
Trick 2: Acid rain chemistry: SO2 + OH → H2SO4; NOx → HNO3, pH < 5.6 — the two acid names earn the mark.
Trick 3: Control devices: electrostatic precipitator (99% particulates), scrubber (SO2 with lime spray), catalytic converter (CO/NOx/unburnt HC) — three devices, three mechanisms.
Trick 4: Delhi-style vehicle control: Bharat/CNG norms, catalytic converters, lead-free petrol — the policy line.
